title: Uncovering Secrets: The Problem of Traumatic Memory
coreMove: Traumatic memory demands humble assessment: weigh arousal, fragments, reenactment, suggestion, and corroboration before belief or dismissal hardens.

exampleSpecs.audience: Adelard, a supervising clinician teaching residents
exampleSpecs.stakes: Residents may dismiss recovered memory debates as only a recent cultural fight.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Pierre Janet's nineteenth-century dissociation work to slow the debate.

exampleSpecs.audience: Rui, an attorney preparing a trauma-sensitive case review
exampleSpecs.stakes: Julian's resurfacing memories involve serious harm and uncertain recall.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hold legal credibility and traumatic fragmentation together.

exampleSpecs.audience: Sukhdeep, a psychiatrist organizing a memory review
exampleSpecs.stakes: The team needs a way to discuss delayed recall without turning intensity into proof.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Weigh time, arousal, suggestibility, and narrative context.

exampleSpecs.audience: Fleur, a therapist reviewing a repeated behavior after group
exampleSpecs.stakes: A repeated action could be dismissed as resistance rather than read carefully.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show reenactment as a clinical clue without making it proof.

exampleSpecs.audience: Imelda, a clerk helping prepare a careful timeline
exampleSpecs.stakes: Thin records can tempt both overconfidence and dismissal.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Keep Julian's priest-abuse allegation open to evidence without forcing certainty.

exampleSpecs.audience: Amara, a therapist preparing for a first session
exampleSpecs.stakes: The session can help integrate fragments or accidentally steer a story.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the talking-cure intuition without turning therapy into a courtroom.
